textbook: Clean cutaway textbook illustration of a SINGLE cardiac PURKINJE FIBRE CELL — a cardiac conducting myocyte from the heart's ventricular conduction system. This is a MUSCLE cell, absolutely NOT a nerve cell: no dendrites, no axon, no myelin, no synapses. Centred in a square 1:1 1080x1080 frame with lots of negative space around the structures for later labels. Fill the whole square edge-to-edge on a neutral dark-charcoal background with NO border, frame, vignette or letterbox. Match the exact house look of a refined educational plate: a MUTED, slightly desaturated palette (soft dusty tints, never bright primary or cartoon colours), THIN clean outlines (not heavy black strokes), gentle soft shading, each structure its own distinct soft colour fill. COMPOSITION: one big, short, blunt BARREL-SHAPED cell fills the centre horizontally, with the abutting blunt ends of its two chain neighbours just entering the frame left and right, so the cells read as a chain joined end to end; a delicate pale grey-blue endocardial lining runs along the very top of the frame just above the chain, and along the bottom a band of NOTICEABLY THINNER, deeper rose-pink, densely cross-striated working cardiomyocytes for size contrast — the Purkinje cell must be clearly two to three times WIDER than those working muscle cells. INTERIOR (quarter cut-away on the central cell): a large PALE CREAM, almost empty, clear glycogen-rich core taking up most of the cell, dusted with soft amber glycogen granules; TWO round muted blue-violet nuclei sitting side by side in the CENTRE of that clear core, each with a small darker nucleolus, surrounded by an obvious pale perinuclear clear halo; SPARSE deeper-rose myofibrils confined to a THIN RING right against the sarcolemma at the cell's outer rim, showing only faint, short cross-striation there and NO striation across the middle of the cell; a scatter of warm-orange mitochondria between the rim myofibrils; fine pale sarcoplasmic-reticulum tubules under the membrane; and at each end-to-end contact a distinct teal-tinted junctional plate of gap junctions drawn as a row of small paired channel cylinders bridging the two membranes. A thin pale connective-tissue sheath wraps the chain. Do NOT draw a neuron, dendrites, an axon, myelin, Nodes of Ranvier or synaptic vesicles. Do NOT draw a flask-shaped cell with a fan-like dendritic tree (that is the unrelated cerebellar Purkinje neuron). Do NOT fill the cell with dense full-width sarcomere banding. Do NOT draw a deep T-tubule system, a cell wall, nucleoid, plasmids, chloroplasts, a large vacuole, cilia or a flagellum, and no lightning bolts, sparks, arrows or glowing trails. Absolutely NO text, letters, numbers, labels, scale bars, arrows or watermarks in the image.
